arguments.narration: The can has a dent and leaks a little at the seam, so the bench gets a stripe and then a puddle. The labels go dark. That is the work.

presentNpcs.name: Ellis Rook
presentNpcs.publicPortrayal: Nineteen, quick, talks with his hands, calls every adult by their first name whether invited or not.

worldFacts: The cool end of the Wrenfield glasshouse holds the potting bench and the seed trays.

function.name: submit_adventure_narration
function.description: Submit short grounded conversational prose for a held turn with no committed mechanics.

cases.input: Ellis asks if the sweet peas are up yet.

arguments.narration: "Not yet," Ellis says, which is what you told him an hour ago. "They'll come. Cold does that to them." He goes back to the trays with both hands full and the conversation finished, which is how conversations go with him. Under the staging, the mice have been at the dropped seed again, and the trays have been squared up by somebody who does not know what a tray is for.

expected.rationale: Two to six sentences, under 120 words, one NPC's voice, and the player left holding their own answer. The length cap is the graded contract here: small models habitually write 400-word set pieces for a conversational beat and drift into writing the player's dialogue.

function.name: submit_adventure_narration

cases.input: I shoulder the seed sack and count what I've recovered of the ledger.

arguments.narration:
You equip 1 burlap seed sack in the back slot. Quest objective advanced for The Dead Graft: recover the lost propagation ledger, now 2 of 3.

The sack goes on the shoulder it was cut for, which is not the shoulder you would have chosen. The recovered pages smell of the seed store, which is a smell you have been trying to get out of your coat since October. Two of three, and the third is somewhere under the hot benches in a language that is not gardening.

Outside the store door the propagating bay ticks its pipe and gets on with it. There is a page still missing, and the cold is not going to improve on it.

expected.rationale: The longer lane allows three or four paragraphs but still caps at 8 sentences and 180 words. Both committed receipts must be stated exactly, and the remaining objective must not be declared finished. Implementation vocabulary is a hard failure in this lane.

function.name: submit_adventure_narration
function.description: Submit short grounded conversational prose for a held turn with no committed mechanics.

cases.input: I walk the whole length of it and see how the frost is coming on.

arguments.narration: You walk it end to end with a hand trailing the pipe the whole way, reading the cold off the iron. The propagating bay is holding. The potting bay has a bloom on the north panes already, thin as breath. By the doorway, where the two drafts meet, there is a finger of ice standing up off the sill like something written and then rubbed out. It will be inside by morning.

expected.rationale: Chat-tuned models add headings, bullets and bold when asked for a structured response, and an 8B asked for 'bounded second-person prose' sometimes decorates it anyway. mustNotInclude turns each markdown form into an individual hard failure, which makes the failure mode legible in the report.

cases.input: The frost is coming in early this year.

arguments.narration: Early this year, and by the north panes already, which is the wrong end to lose first. You will lose the other end too inside a fortnight, and the palms will argue about it. The heat pipe ticks its one note along the whole run and is not going to be argued with.

expected.rationale: The narration lane enforces exactly one envelope call with no siblings and no content-only answer. Llama-3.1-8B in particular tends to emit both a tool call and loose prose, or to answer with content alone. This case measures the discipline rather than the writing.

function.name: submit_adventure_narration

cases.input: I cross the walk and nod him good evening.

arguments.narration: Haldane takes the nod the way he takes everything: without moving any part of his face. He is looking at the north panes, and at the finger of ice on the sill, and he has been looking at them long enough that you already know what he is going to say. He does not say it. He taps the pipe with one knuckle and goes back down the walk, and the glass goes on letting the cold in around the edges.

expected.rationale: The controlled actor is addressed as 'you' and never re-enters the cast. mustNotInclude blocks third-person self-reference, which is the specific drift that appears when a character card supplies both a name and a description, and blocks gendering a character the setup never gendered.

cases.input: I ask Ellis what he thinks the estate is doing with the seed store.

arguments.narration: Ellis considers this with his hands, which means he turns a pot a quarter turn twice. "Nothing," he says. "That's the thing. It's not shut and it's not open, it's just nobody's business any more." He sets the pot down square. "Haldane's the only one who still goes in, and he won't say why, and if you ask him he'll tell you about the frost."

expected.rationale: Screenplay and chat-log formatting is a very common small-model reflex and it destroys the prose illusion. Dialogue belongs in quotation marks inside a narrated paragraph, attributed by action rather than by a name colon.

cases.input: Nothing much. Just the frost and the long walk home.

arguments.narration: That is most of it. The walk home is four miles along the wall and takes an hour at the pace you keep, and tonight the ice is coming in on the north side of every pane in the row, so the glass is a mirror and the mirror is out past the wall and the wall is out past the field. You take your time anyway.

expected.rationale: A low-content turn is the one that makes small models reach outside the frame and start being helpful. mustNotInclude pins assistant-voice leakage ('as the DM', 'your turn', 'let me know') and refusal language. The correct reply is a short grounded beat and nothing else.
